source.title: Discovering and forecasting extreme events via active learning in neural operators
source.authors: Ethan M. Pickering; S. Guth; G. Karniadakis; T. Sapsis

record.tranche_reason: The study reports a sample-wise double-descent pattern for some acquisition methods and says its proposed sampling method avoids that pattern in the 20D example, refining the claim by showing dependence on data selection.
record.gate_note: The study tests sample-wise change in log-PDF error as training samples are acquired. It does not test model-size or epoch-wise curves. Results about an 8D parallel study are cited rather than reported as this study's own results and are excluded. Other figures comparing error trajectories are not described in the text as showing double descent.
record.test_reason: In a new setting (DeepONet surrogates trained by active learning on the 20D MMT wave problem), the study reports that log-PDF test error rises as more samples are acquired under LHS and US sampling. The authors link this to sample-wise double descent. That is a direct, if loosely measured, result on V3. Under the authors' own US-LW acquisition the rise does not appear. The study does not locate an interpolation threshold, and the evidence is figure-only.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Authors state that US-LW 'eliminates' sample-wise double descent in the 20D example, while LHS and US worsen with more data. They hedge that this 'appears to be related' to double descent. They defer the mechanism (uninformative data adding misleading complexity) to a parallel study [41], not to their own results.
record.recipe_differences: Uses active learning with DeepONet and alternative acquisition strategies, measuring log-PDF error as data are acquired; it does not reproduce the original model-size or epoch sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: In the 20D example, the reported sample-wise error behavior depends on acquisition strategy: US-LW avoids double descent, while other acquisition functions worsen with more acquired data. The authors report similar US-LW error metrics for initial data with and without extremes.
record.problems: The 20D true PDF is not definitively converged: the authors state that doing so would require more than 10^7 samples and base their truth metric on 10^5 test samples. The reported metric is log-PDF error rather than conventional pointwise test error, and no interpolation threshold is identified.
record.rows_left_out: No additional double-descent rows were extracted from Figure 3 because the text does not describe those trajectories as showing double descent. The cited parallel study's findings are not this study's own results.

untested.parts: No interpolation threshold is located. There is no evidence the rise sits near it, and a second descent is not shown explicitly. Pointwise test error (MSE) is not reported in this study; it is only cited from parallel work [41].
No capacity sweep across model classes.
No label-noise, multiple-peak or regularization tests.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed from T5 to T3: the study does not argue that V3 is wrong; it reports the effect in a new setting and shows that data selection removes it. The 20D ground-truth PDF is not fully converged (10^5 test samples). Rows from 2D-8D, SIR and LAMP show no double descent claims. The 8D MSE double-descent results belong to cited work [41] and are not rows.

versions.untested_parts: No test-error sweep over training epochs.
The study measures log-PDF approximation error, not conventional pointwise test loss, and does not locate an interpolation threshold or establish that the increase occurs near it.
No capacity sweep across model classes past an interpolation point.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested against peak locations.
No test of label-noise dependence, multiple peaks, or optimally tuned regularization.
No alternative effective-parameter count is used to assess whether the curve becomes an ordinary U-shape.

rows.subject: DNO (DeepONet)
rows.operation_detail: Increase acquired training samples using likelihood-weighted uncertainty sampling (US-LW).
rows.measure: Log-PDF error between the surrogate and true output distributions as acquired sample count increases
rows.note: The authors state that US-LW avoids log-PDF error double descent in the 20D problem. The figure compares initial-data regimes; the authors report similar error metrics for initial data with and without extremes.
rows.check: This is the study's proposed acquisition method, set against the comparators. It selects non-random, targeted data, so its absence reflects a data-selection choice. It is not a failure of more data to hurt under ordinary sampling.

rows.subject: DNO (DeepONet)
rows.operation_detail: Increase acquired training samples using uncertainty sampling (US).

conditions.value: prior px and LHS regimes shown

rows.measure: Log-PDF error between the surrogate and true output distributions as acquired sample count increases
rows.note: The authors say the other acquisition functions perform worse as more data are acquired and associate this behavior with sample-wise double descent.
rows.check: Figure-only evidence. Text says error gets 'worse as more data is acquired'. No interpolation threshold is identified, and the authors only say the pattern 'appears to be related' to double descent. The measure is log-PDF error of the output distribution, not pointwise test loss.

rows.subject: DNO (DeepONet)
rows.operation_detail: Increase training samples using Latin hypercube sampling (LHS).
rows.measure: Log-PDF error between the surrogate and true output distributions as sample count increases
rows.note: The authors say the other acquisition functions perform worse as more data are acquired and associate this behavior with sample-wise double descent.
rows.check: Same caveats as dd20_us. LHS is the closest analogue to random i.i.d. sampling, so this is the most relevant row for V3.

relationships.condition: 20D MMT, DeepONet ensemble (N=2), LHS and US sampling
relationships.reason: Authors report log-PDF error worsening as more data are acquired, which they link to sample-wise double descent (dd20_us, dd20_lhs). The evidence is figure-only and no threshold is located.
relationships.display_finding: Log-density error worsened as more data were acquired under both sampling methods, without a located interpolation threshold.

relation.reason: The study reports more-data harm under LHS and US and its avoidance under US-LW, directly bearing on V3.

tranche.reason: Own sample-scaling results in a new setting: active learning of 20D MMT dynamics with DeepONet. The study explicitly compares acquisition-dependent error trajectories.

source_check.notes: Evidence establishes acquisition-dependent more-data harm, without numerical rise values or a measured interpolation threshold. Table 1 changes branch depth from five to six above 2,500 samples; Section 4.3 uses a shared finite test-set KDE rather than a definitively converged 20D reference PDF.

statements.correction: Own result: 20D MMT log-PDF error worsens with additional LHS or US samples; interpolation threshold unmeasured. MSE-double-descent elimination: cited parallel 8D study [41]. Peer-review status: unverified from supplied text.
statements.problem: The log-PDF-error finding, comparisons and uncertainty reporting are supported; peer-review status is not established by the supplied arXiv text. The MSE double-descent result is attributed to parallel study [41].
